description: A hub item for the participant is taken into the local queue, picked up there, and its result closes it on the hub.
recordedFrom: The network connector of @openrig/cli 0.7.23 against a hub that answers application/json (never SSE). Seats, ids, times and texts are synthetic.

placeholders.<TOKEN>: The participant's bearer: the token the test gives the binding.
placeholders.<REQUEST_ITEM>: The hub item id the connector derives for an outbound request (bound from the first request that names one).
placeholders.<TIME>: Any ISO time in a request (a local claim time in a pickup note, say).

passes.does: Take: the pending list names the item (without its body), the connector claims it, shows it for the body, and notes it queued.
The local seat picked it up and closed it done: pickup note, a check that the hub item is still open, the close, and its readback.
After the close: nothing held, nothing pending, nothing more is written.

result.instructions:
Discover the team this grant connects you to by calling rig_team without rigId. A sole granted rig is selected automatically; with several, it returns the granted names to choose from.
This server reaches an OpenRig team as one seat: the one named by OPENRIG_SESSION_NAME where the server was configured, or, over authenticated HTTP, the seat of the caller's grant (rig_team shows a rig's seats and its lead). The daemon attributes this server's writes to that seat.
To hand work to a seat, use rig_queue_create and keep its qitemId; read the answer later with rig_queue_show, which names the next item when the work was handed on. Queue items are durable: they outlive this conversation and this server.
Tools marked read-only change nothing. A seat whose activity is unknown is not idle, and an accepted request (a restore's attemptId) is not a finished one.
A question reserved for a person is theirs to answer: don't answer it on their behalf.
Acceptance is not completed work. Choose a qitemId and pass it to rig_queue_create, so an uncertain create (a timeout, or an error after sending) can be checked: read that same qitemId with rig_queue_show first, and create again only with that same id, never a new one.
Items addressed to your seat are yours: rig_queue_list with owned set lists them. For each, claim it (rig_queue_claim), do it, then close it done with closure reason no-follow-on and the answer in resolution (rig_queue_update); the sender reads that answer on the same item. A message is an item too: read it and close it done, with your reply in resolution when it needs one; its sender reads that reply on the same item. Nothing promises to wake you, so check your items again.
Before sending a request to another assistant, list the team's members. If more than one could be the one your person means, ask which, using their names from the list (like "Sam's Claude"); if the list shows only addresses, describe each in plain words from what the list says about it (like "the Claude chat agent"), never reading the address out. Don't pick from your own history or memory. If the list shows the chosen one detached or stopped, or a connected assistant with no check-in yet or overdue, say so before sending and ask whether to send it anyway. If the list says the chosen one's person is no longer on the team, don't send; tell your person and ask whether to send it to someone else. When you send to another connected assistant, tell your person how it picks requests up as the list says (when its person asks it, or on its check-in schedule); if the list doesn't say, say that's unknown, and don't promise a time. If your person names one clearly, or says to send it anyway to one that isn't connected, go ahead without asking again. If your person still asks to send to one whose person is no longer on the team, tell them it can't be delivered: requests to an assistant whose person is no longer on the team are closed unanswered.
